notes.title: Realpolitiks 3: Earth and Beyond Leaves Early Access!
notes.content:
Greetings, fellow leaders!

The day has finally come, allow us to officially announce that [b]Realpolitiks 3: Earth and Beyond leaves Early Access today[/b] and launches as a full game, [b]being 20% off at launch[/b].

On this opportunity, Realpolitiks II is getting a discount too. You can get it with [b]85% off[/b].

[previewyoutube=gZJraraQprQ;full][/previewyoutube]

First of all, we'd like to start with a huge "thank you" to every single one of you for taking part in the Early Access journey, whether it was by purchasing the game, participating in the Open Beta, writing a review here on Steam or simply sharing your comments on the forums. It is you, our community, that helped us get through and shape the game.

Now to the full launch itself. The game features a whole host of new content and updates for its 1.0 launch today. These include:

[list]
[*] [b]A new "Climate War" scenario[/b], in which the world faces a wave of climate disasters, eventually leading to a new type of wars to emerge, with countries fighting for basic resources and survival.
[*] [b]Finalized Leadership mechanic[/b], letting players develop their Head of State and other members of the cabinet as they gain experience.
[*] Various quality of life features, improvements and bugfixes based on community feedback, including the Timeline review, in which players can see how successful their reign has been, new combat balancing and changes to trade functionality, among others.
[*] Localization to [b]German, Spanish, French, Polish, Simplified Chinese and Russian[/b] languages.
[*] Option to utilise the cash reserves to purchase the main resources at market prices.
[/list]

Besides that, we’ve implemented tons of fixes and changes, including updates of the difficulty levels. The whole Change Log and more details about the full launch can be found [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2298690/view/519711795144818848]in the original announcement[/url].

Don't forget that the game is also included in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/46403/Realpolitiks_Franchise_Bundle/]REALPOLITIKS FRANCHISE[/url] bundle along with its older siblings where you can get an additional bundle discount.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/46403/Realpolitiks_Franchise_Bundle/

If you have not done so yet, hop in to the [url=https://discord.gg/ZwXekHkTDK]Realpolitiks HQ Discord server[/url] as well!

Thank you again for being a part of this journey with us!

Happy Strategizing!

In the demo, you will be thrown right into the middle of a deadly epidemic of the Iron Plague - select from 2 classes and play as either a Voodoo Shaman or a Diesel Engineer of either the Human or Elven race, and investigate what's going on in the Leprosarium; a hospital specializing in treating patients in the Slums district suffering from the horrific disease. https://store.steampowered.com/app/2458310/New_Arc_Line/

The demo will allow you to govern either Germany or Mexico, and you will have 5 in-game years to show off your cunning leadership skills in the new, extreme Overdrive mode. At launch, any contemporary nation will be available for your ambitions, from Afghanistan to Zimbabwe and everything in between, and you will be able to enjoy different campaign modes to boot!

notes.title: Realpolitiks II Update Live and More News about the Franchise!
notes.content:
Greetings, world leaders!

We have amazing news for you today: Thanks to our work on the new sequel, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2298690/Realpolitiks_3_Earth_and_Beyond/]Realpolitiks 3: Earth and Beyond[/url], we have been able to incorporate some of the newly developed tools and technologies to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1248060/Realpolitiks_II/]Realpolitiks II[/url], fixing a major issue that we have not been able to address before - the dreaded time-freeze bug. This will prevent any new occurrences of the bug, but if your game has already been affected by it, you may unfortunately have to load an earlier save or start a new game, as not every save file will be fixed. Besides squashing this major bug, we looked into minor rebalancing of AI and other small fixes as well.

We will be looking for even more opportunities to use the tools and engine upgrades newly developed for [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2298690/Realpolitiks_3_Earth_and_Beyond/]Realpolitiks 3: Earth and Beyond[/url] to improve the original games as well. We hope to prove to you that the development of the new game is good news for the franchise overall; while we are pushing the series forward with the new installment, we do not want to just forget about its roots.

[h3]New Details about Realpolitiks 3: Earth and Beyond[/h3]

However, we also want to make full use of the new engine and bring forth features and gameplay options that simply are not possible to implement into the originals. We would like to take a moment to introduce some of the many possibilities you can look forward to when the game launches later this year. That is why we have prepared a first in the series of devlogs - check it out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2298690/view/4352251596693173112]here[/url].

We will be sharing even more news and sneak peeks soon - if you want to stay up to date, wishlist the game here on Steam and come join us on the official [url=https://discord.com/invite/6d7pNK2]Realpolitiks HQ Discord server[/url], we would love to hear what you think!

We will see you on the world stage soon - on Earth, in space, and beyond!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2298690/Realpolitiks_3_Earth_and_Beyond/

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/e711e9067c88bfe8c1ef4d680f9c1f62148afa35.png[/img]

Hello everyone! We have an announcement regarding the big update that was scheduled for release today. As mentioned before, it’s a huge update that deals with some of the most severe bugs in the game and it’s something the development team has worked on really hard for the last month. We really wanted to bring it your way as soon as we could; unfortunately, just as we were coming to a close of the testing process we have stumbled upon a rare, but quite impactful bug. The team did its best to diagnose and eliminate it, but it seems that we weren’t able to pinpoint its causes accurately enough to get rid of it completely in this brief period of time. 

We know that you - our community - were more than patient with us during those past few months and we hate to tell you that we need to delay a feature once more; however we feel that this is the best choice, with the alternative being rolling out a release that can potentially introduce a new, serious issue.
For now, we haven’t had the time to gather enough data to give you a new estimated release date for this update. We will inform you of any news as soon as we can. Once again, thank you so much for your patience and understanding.

notes.title: Dev blog #6 - Warfare
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/689c56dd6e89271a5dd81d7e916c2c5feea15908.png[/img]

Hey everyone,

Today we’ve got an exciting issue of our Dev Blog and we are going to dive in to explore how warfare works in Realpolitiks II, so let’s get going:

Let’s start from the beginning by introducing units, shall we?

[h3]Units[/h3]

There are three types of units in Realpolitiks II: land, air, and sea. Each force has several units, such as infantry, commandos, militia, artillery, tanks, fighters, bombers, helicopters, submarines, corvettes and aircraft carriers. Each unit has a different attack, defense, and support parameter against other units.

Units are grouped into armies that you can move around the world map. An army can only move in neutral provinces (such as international waters, or uninhabited lands like on the poles), provinces that you own and those of your allies - both from the bloc and those with which you have signed military access). In the event of war, once an army reaches an enemy province it begins to occupy it - tipping the scales of victory in your favor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/a100c9c2bf2b8074883756f1fefbaa8c8ee4fe59.png[/img]

With the help of design and technology, units can be developed into state-specific units, such as Spetsnaz in Russia or the Soryu ship in Japan.

As a part of our in-game video tutorials - here you can learn more about navigating the barracks and recruiting more units:

[previewyoutube=iSpSwg4qrbI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Generals[/h3]

Armies can be commanded by generals who give them additional combat skills, improve their stats, or reduce army costs. Generals, like spies, have 2 development paths - land and sea. Depending on which army the general is assigned to and what battles he wins, the more experience from that particular level he gains. After each level, you will be able to select one of two available random perks for him.

[h3]Land Theaters[/h3]

If two different enemy armies are in the same land province, a combat theater will begin. Each province has a different battlefield, depending on the terrain, you will find cities, villages, forests, mountains, clearings, rivers, lakes and more. Some units cannot move in specific areas (e.g. tanks do not go into the mountains), but planes have no restrictions. During combat, you can take control of each unit and decide where to move and who to attack - remember that success comes from many factors, such as the general's level, unit statistics, distance to the target, type of field on which units are standing and many more. It is also important whether the units are standing next to each other and whether they have a clear line of fire - it is not difficult to accidentally hit an ally. The efficiency of units is also influenced by the weather and actions in the theater - that is, properly issued commands that can give a short-lasting boost to attack, defense, or speed. Reserves management is also important in combat - if you receive reinforcements during a battle, you must make sure that they will be able to participate in combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/65e5e5be76c81b20da606512d1dfd963b45dc80f.png[/img]

[h3]Sea Theaters[/h3]

On the other hand, if two armies meet at sea, the course of the whole fight may be quite different - first of all, the naval forces have the advantage here, but the support of aircraft is also invaluable. Land units at sea are transported in ordinary barges, meaning their strength and vitality are abysmal - if you don’t take care of the proper protection of your tanks and infantry, they will quickly become cannon fodder. On the water, you can also find islands and shoals that change the parameter of all units.

[h3]Alert State[/h3]

During a battle, the level of combat readiness is extremely important. The lower it is the greater the country's focus on military production - unfortunately, this takes place at the expense of the economy, so countries focused primarily on the military can easily go bankrupt. Different policy systems have different requirements to advance to the next alert state level. Nevertheless, it is worth the risk as higher levels allow you to use more lethal rockets, including dirty bombs, and significantly increase the number of recruits and the speed of unit recruitment.

[h3]Nuclear Warfare[/h3]

There is no superpower in the world without its dose of atom. Countries now have a wide variety of missiles, ranging from ordinary missiles, to nuclear and biological weapons, to chemical weapons. For missile production, it is necessary to build silos which also act as anti-missile systems. When choosing the target of the attack, the player can determine the size of the load, and thus the extent of damage and its strength. Just remember that this type of attack affects not only the target, but also its surroundings, so if you drop a bomb on Lichtenstein, you will definitely hurt Germany and France - thus making friends with them will be that much more difficult...

That’s it! Warfare is definitely a fascinating topic, so we cannot wait to see you play your hearts out with dominating the globe with your military. As always guys, if you have a question or suggestion - be sure to leave a comment or create a thread in the Steam discussions, or join our Discord channel to hang out!

Oh, and don’t forget to wishlist the game! 

Until next time!

notes.title: #4 Dev blog - Spies
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Welcome to the next Realpolitiks II developer blog! This time we are focusing on espionage and how you can use it to gain more information on your opponents. Let’s dive in:

[h3]Recruit spies and develop intelligence agencies[/h3]

Politics in the real world as well as in Realpolitiks II could not exist without some form of espionage. In the second installment we developed and enhanced the intelligence mechanics by adding spy units that can play a pivotal role in knowing what your opponents are doing and whether or not you should feel threatened. Spies' abilities, their number, movement speed, preparation time, and mission execution depend on the amount of time and resources you have invested in the intelligence agency. The spy network can be developed either through buildings or projects (please note though that the project window is not final).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/f61e833504664e21b321de58160133020b05e91a.png[/img]
[h3]Lead the spies[/h3]

Each spy is an individual unit on the map that you can send out on a mission. After reaching its destination, the spy begins to prepare for the mission, creating spy networks, and infiltrating the enemy structures gaining espionage points over time. The more points he gets, the more powerful actions he will be able to perform and the greater the likelihood of successful actions. Also, the more spies in the same place, the faster you earn espionage points. Enemy spies can slow down the infiltration, or even completely prevent it - in which case the only solution is to carry out the mission elsewhere.

The spy has a full name and an avatar that you can modify in any way during the game. Recruited spies have a name and surname typical for a given country or culture - for example, when playing as the United States you will not find Chinese names among your spies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/297f21463fbb4298ef41dcf8ccd4c49268e7ed5a.png[/img]
[h3]Gain experience and skills[/h3]

Each spy gains experience points for completed missions, which will allow him to level up and gain additional skills, including the ability to perform new missions. Spies can reach 6 levels, and with each level you will have to choose one of two randomly chosen skills. There are around 80 unique skills in total, so to benefit from all of them you will need an army of well-trained agents. Lots of options here!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/e1d0b95072b4810f5c8c3297ed94fe883dc0d5ea.png[/img]
[h3]Conduct intelligence and counterintelligence activities[/h3]

You can use spies in two ways - to fight your enemies or to strengthen your power in the country. Each spy has two independent paths of development - intelligence and counter-intelligence. Depending on whether you use the spy to counteract hostile actions in your country or to weaken your enemies,  the development will progress in a specific direction. The action repertoire includes about 80 activities, such as:
[list]
[*] Intimidating Politicians
[*] Manipulating the Stock Exchange
[*] Faking an Assassination
[*] Compromising the Government
[*] LGBT Promotion
[*] Conspiring with Communists
[*] Troll Hiring
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/f6ef2356ea99980a4fec1013c9a4337eca2e8b51.png[/img]
[h3]Mod Tool[/h3]

With the modding tool you can edit every aspect of the spy. You decide on the number of levels, experience points, skills, and spy actions. There will also be an editor for names and surnames for a given country or culture, which will enable you to modify the lists of names randomly assigned to characters from the game. For each action you will be able to set the effects, requirements, costs, and description.

That’s it! This concludes the development blog and we would like to know your thoughts on the espionage system? Any strategies to conquer your opponents? Let us know in the comments! Also please add Realpolitiks II to your wishlist as it helps us a ton! Thank you!

[b]Thank you for reading and we will see you in the next one![/b]

notes.title: #3 Dev blog - Policies, Projects and Modding tools
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We’re back at it again with another Developer Blog! This time we’re going to feature the policies of our selected country, a little info about projects, and something exciting with what the Mod Tool is going to offer! Let’s dive in:

[h3]Internal Policy[/h3]

Following the example of the first Realpolitiks we decided to leave the game's three basic political systems: democracy, authoritarianism, and totalitarianism. Each system allows you to take different actions, which is why playing with democracy is very different from playing with a totalitarian state. Political systems affect available actions in provinces, actions in the region, buildings, projects, diplomatic and espionage actions, and negotiations. That sounds like a lot, but there’s more! Political systems depend on the level of Interventionism, Militarism and Personal Control. These, in turn, are determined by the buildings operating in your country, active actions in the respective regions and provinces, projects introduced and decisions made during events. Tons of decisions have to be made for you to be successful on your journey to dominance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/ce0380ea7be45009e2730d1c0a3c6011265b2152.png[/img]

[h3]Political parties[/h3]

Political parties are new to Realpolitiks II. After each election, i.e. with the change of the system, the power distribution in the parliament changes. The parties play a very important role in the game - everything depends on their decisions whether you can perform specific actions, place buildings, introduce decrees, or develop new and existing technology. Political parties will be able to block the possibility of declaring a war or sending a specific proposal during peace negotiations. Also, if the majority in the parliament will be held by democratic parties, you will not get permission to build collective farms for example. Totalitarian parties will gladly support such actions, but they prevent you from relinquishing a province to another country, even if you lose the war. Of course, it wouldn’t have been politics without party bribing - some views become more flexible if the parliamentarians have their pockets full. By lobbying, you can persuade the party to change their mind, although in some cases even this may not be enough and your hands will be tied until the next election.
The more democratic your country is, the greater the strength of the democratic parties will be. If you remain a democracy, but you are on the threshold of authoritarianism, it is possible that more totalitarian parties will win the elections, which will open up a number of opportunities for countries with a different system.
The number of parties entering the parliament also depends on the political system - in a democracy the number of seats is diversified, while in totalitarianism you will meet only one. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/2c2b2f5a2fa8a0a1bebbcfa96a5a77f736bb0fe8.png[/img]

[h3]Political projects[/h3]

As part of the project trees, we have prepared numerous solutions that will allow you to give your country an individual character, using various political and economic doctrines, and social projects. Do you want to remain a democracy focused on the cult of the leader and full capitalism that exploits the citizens? Nothing stands in the way. Are you going to create a communist utopia? Or maybe you want to play as a totalitarian state that does not maintain an army and allocates all resources to social and economic activities? Will you choose a geopolitical player who will become a world sheriff integrating in every war, or will you create an isolated enclave without any diplomatic relations? You are only limited by your fantasy and your country's budget. And maybe some political parties would be a little problem, but an experienced leader like you can handle them, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/c35f5f1215de1e0975dfc2b95d20a7c4f5b024c5.png[/img]

[h3]Mod tool[/h3]

As part of the modding tool you can determine the influence of Interventionism, Militarism and Personal Control on political systems in your own scenarios. If you want, nothing prevents you from creating a game in which there are only totalitarian states.
You will be given full freedom to create political parties and their programs. It will be up to you how many political parties enter parliament during elections - do you want 50 parties to operate in the country, and 20 in the parliament? No problem, although such governments can be quite troublesome for you.

Nothing prevents you from using the mod tool to define which actions are available to specific systems. You will also have full freedom in shaping project trees as you see fit, so if you decide that you want to extend the personalization of political systems, e.g. introducing the institution of a vice king to the country, seizing power as dictator in times of danger, creating a purely religious state that believes in aliens - you will be able to introduce these types of projects and actions into the game.

This concludes the latest issue of our development blog! The release date is coming closer and we’re extremely excited preparing Realpolitiks II for that special day. Let us know your thoughts in the comments and we will see you in the very next entry! And if you haven’t done so already, please don’t forget to add the game to your Steam wishlist!

Until next time!

notes.title: #1 Dev blog - The world, nations, scenarios and more!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/169429f2b0af1be823491bdc85364d7c13c33139.jpg[/img]

Hello everyone,

Welcome to the very [b]first Development Blog[/b] of Realpolitiks II in which we will showcase some inside information about our upcoming Grand Strategy game. Don’t worry if you haven’t played the first Realpolitiks as we will develop a set of tutorials that will give you all the necessary tools and knowledge for you to start conquering the world. Now then, let’s get it started, shall we?

[b]Coronavirus Pandemic[/b]
Just a little heads up as Jujubee has switched into working remotely. Everything is planned for the duration of the pandemic and we haven’t experienced any delays in our work whatsoever. We would just like to ask everyone to practice social distancing and stay home for as long as it takes in hopes of waiting out this pesky virus. Let’s all stay safe out there and be responsible.

[b]The World of Realpolitiks II[/b]
We thought it would be a good idea to start the very first Development Blog by introducing you to the world itself. To new players reading this segment, Realpolitiks 2 takes place on the world map where you see your selected nation and its neighbors (your neighbors). The vast majority of gameplay will be on this very screen where you choose how you will manage your nation in this quest for world dominance. So, let’s talk about provinces which are the main points of administration in the game.

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/c8e37980931ff19fc3bc27babadf8d26855d5395.jpg[/img]

Provinces provide us with citizens, taxes, GDP, and resources. You can perform certain actions in each province so that you can gain some extra income or resources for a little while. What’s new in Realpolitiks II is the addition of buildings and their purpose is to grant certain benefits by placing them in a province. Beginners and veterans alike should enjoy this added feature as it greatly expands on the number of tactical approaches you can make while planning out your plan. Remember though, only one building per province, so place them strategically (you can always demolish and place a new one, but it will cost you - and money is important). 

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/696f3e5fa957f70dbc126037c454ff6e21d8ba79.jpg[/img]

A group of provinces create a region. And regions are independent of nations - meaning they can be divided by a couple of countries. It is in each country’s business to control a full region as uniting all provinces grants the option of issuing decrees that boost overall production.

Those were land provinces, note that you will also encounter territorial waters that are located along the coast. You won’t get citizens from them, but they can provide you with resources and you can place special buildings such as shipyards or oil rigs.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/4a8f1cceea5ffcfb6039fef5af767279fcf2f031.jpg[/img]

Also, we’ve got to take into account the international waters as they are not a part of any country and anyone can freely pass through them - at least to the point when the waters are not colonized, as then countries can build artificial islands, underwater bases, or other helpful structures.

[b]Nations & Scenarios[/b]
In Realpolitiks II you are the nation. You will always remain in control, despite the election results. This would have been a bad design decision to have players conduct their operations and then the decision-making ability would be taken away because of elections. You are always in control. Hopefully we’ve shed some light on this subject. Now then, let’s continue. We’ve thought this is something worth mentioning as we have seen you guys asking about it a lot.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36992101/04183bc08fd464dff64f574f882d51a003e356de.jpg[/img]

Countries have varying sizes - from small island nations to Russia spreading across two continents. You will be able to play as the Vatican, or other countries that are not recognized by most of the population, like Sealand. Each country begins at a different technological, political, economic, and military level, but each one of them is playable. Of course, the game provides you with the option to play in sandbox mode, but if someone prefers to have clearly set goals then we’ve got you covered. Step right up to the Great Campaign where we will give you fixed goals to achieve world dominance - be it through diplomacy, conquests, or technology.

In addition, special scenarios have been prepared depending on the size of the country. We’ve also got scenarios that occur only when playing a specific country, e.g. the USA, China, Russia, France, Spain, Italy, etc. 

###

That’s a wrap of our first Developer Blog for Realpolitiks II. We are always listening to your suggestions and ideas, so don’t hesitate to share them with us! You can leave a comment here or on the Steam discussions, and remember we’ve got a Discord channel dedicated to Realpolitiks. If you feel like joining - then by all means!

Thank you for reading and we will see you in the next one!

Wishlist now:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1248060/Realpolitiks_II/

- Jujubee Team
